KSIs.ksiStatement: Modifications to the cloud service offering are logged and monitored.
Changes to machine-based information resources are executed through the redeployment of version controlled resources rather than direct modification wherever reasonable.
The effectiveness of documented change management procedures is persistently reviewed.
Persistent testing and validation of changes throughout deployment is automated.
The functionality and privileges for infrastructure and services are strictly defined.
Automated services are used to persistently assess the security of all machine-based information resources and automatically enforce their intended operational state.
The use and configuration of third-party machine-based information resources is persistently compared against the original provider's best practices and guidance.
Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they have a minimal attack surface and that lateral movement is minimized if compromised.
Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they are appropriately optimized for high availability and rapid recovery.
Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they are appropriately configured to limit inbound and outbound network traffic.
The effectiveness of protection against denial of service attacks and other unwanted activity for machine-based information resources is persistently reviewed.
Logical networking and related capabilities are used and persistently reviewed to enforce traffic flow controls.

The effectiveness of relevant cybersecurity education and training is persistently reviewed, including at least general training for all employees, role-specific training for employees in high risk roles, training for development and engineering staff on secure software delivery, and training for staff involved with incident response or disaster recovery.
The lifecycle and privileges of all accounts, roles, and groups are securely managed using automation.
Secure passwordless methods are used for user authentication and authorization when feasible, otherwise strong passwords with phishing-resistant MFA is used.
Identity and access management measures are used and persistently reviewed to ensure each user or device can only access the resources they need.
A least-privileged, role and attribute-based, and just-in-time security authorization model is used and persistently reviewed for all user and non-user accounts and services.
Appropriately secure authentication methods are used and persistently reviewed for non-user accounts and services.
Accounts with privileged access are disabled or otherwise secured in response to suspicious activity.
Incident after action reports are generated and lessons learned are persistently incorporated.
The effectiveness of documented incident response procedures is persistently reviewed.
Past incidents are persistently reviewed for patterns or vulnerabilities that were not previously apparent or identified.
A least-privileged, role and attribute-based, and just-in-time access authorization model is used and persistently reviewed for access to log data based on organizationally defined data sensitivity.
The configuration of machine-based information resources, especially infrastructure as code, is persistently evaluated and tested.
A list of information resources and event types that will be logged, monitored, and audited is maintained and persistently reviewed to ensure these activities occur.
A Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) or similar system(s) is used and persistently reviewed for centralized, tamper-resistant logging of events, activities, and changes.
Logs are persistently reviewed and audited.
Authoritative sources are used to automatically generate real-time inventories of all information resources when needed.
Executive support for achieving the provider's security goals is persistently reviewed and demonstrated.
The effectiveness of the provider's investments in achieving security goals is persistently reviewed.
The effectiveness of building security and privacy considerations into the Software Development Lifecycle and aligning with CISA Secure By Design principles is persistently reviewed.
The effectiveness of the provider's vulnerability disclosure program is persistently reviewed.
The alignment of machine-based information resource backups with defined recovery objectives is persistently reviewed.
The alignment of recovery plans with defined recovery objectives is persistently reviewed.
The desired Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) are defined and persistently reviewed for alignment with the provider's business needs and capabilities.
The capability to recover from incidents and contingencies aligned with defined recovery objectives is persistently tested.
The configuration of machine-based information resources is managed using automation and persistently reviewed for drift.
Management, protection, and regular rotation of digital keys, certificates, and other secrets is automated and persistently reviewed.
Information resources are persistently evaluated for opportunities to improve security and those improvements are persistently made.

Plans, procedures, and the state of information resources are persistently reviewed after making changes to limit and remove unwanted residual elements that would likely negatively affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of federal customer data.

Unwanted federal customer data is removed promptly when requested by an agency in alignment with customer agreements, including from backups if appropriate; this typically applies when a customer spills information or when a customer seeks to remove information from a service due to a change in usage.
Information is encrypted or otherwise secured from unwanted access or modification.
The authenticity and integrity of communications between machine-based information resources is persistently validated using automation.
Use cryptographic methods to validate the integrity of machine-based information resources.
Persistently identify, review, and mitigate potential supply chain risks.

Third party software information resources are automatically monitored for upstream vulnerabilities using mechanisms that may include contractual notification requirements or active monitoring services.

Rev5_controls.title: Policy and Procedures
Rev5_controls.statement:
a. Develop, document, and disseminate to [organization-defined personnel or roles]:
    1. [organization-level OR mission/business process-level OR system-level] access control policy that:
      (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and
      (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and
    2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the access control policy and the associated access controls;
  b. Designate an [official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the access control policy and procedures; and
  c. Review and update the current access control:
    1. Policy [frequency] and following [events] ; and
    2. Procedures [frequency] and following [events].
Rev5_controls.rationale:
No KSIs reflect control satisfaction.

This control's Automatable rating improves from NONE (0) to FAIR (2) with agentic AI: An agentic AI could review the access-control policy document to confirm it exists, is approved, and covers the required elements, rather than this being a purely manual review. This raises the aggregated coverage score from 0 to 0.

Rev5_controls.title: Account Management
Rev5_controls.rationale: 3 of 4 mapped KSIs provide some evidence: KSI-IAM-JIT (STRONG); KSI-IAM-SNU (FAIR); KSI-IAM-SUS (FAIR). Rev5_controls.title: Managed Access Control Points

Mapping.prerequisites: Requires network infrastructure (VPN/ZTNA gateway) configuration to be queryable via API to confirm all remote access routes through designated control points.

Mapping.rationale: Wireless-specific authentication/encryption only applies where wireless is in use and is a narrow slice of the broader attack-surface/lateral-movement concern.
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires wireless access point/controller configuration to be queryable via API for authentication/encryption settings.

Mapping.rationale: Disabling unused wireless capability is a narrow, wireless-specific hardening action rather than a general attack-surface/lateral-movement control.

Mapping.rationale: This enhancement sets conditions for permitting external system use; it's more about authorization terms than minimizing attack surface or lateral movement.

Mapping.ai_description: An agentic AI could read external-system connection agreements/attestations and check for the required verification language, rather than this being a purely manual contract review.

Mapping.rationale: Authorizing and documenting internal connections directly supports limiting the paths available for lateral movement, a core piece of the KSI's stated intent.

Mapping.ai_description: Beyond enumerating connections via network tooling, an agentic AI could reconcile that list against authorization records to confirm each connection is both documented and approved.

Mapping.rationale: Limiting the number of external network connections directly reduces exposed attack surface - a core, direct match.
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires network topology/firewall management tooling that can enumerate all external connection points via API.

Mapping.rationale: Managed interfaces and traffic-flow policy at external boundaries support attack-surface reduction, though this control is broader (covers policy/confidentiality/integrity) than surface minimization alone.

Mapping.rationale: Denying traffic by default and allowing only by exception directly minimizes exposed attack surface - a core, direct mechanism.
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires firewall/security-group configuration to be queryable via API to confirm a default-deny posture with explicit exception rules.

Mapping.rationale: Routing traffic through authenticated proxies reduces direct exposure of internal resources, a relevant but narrower mechanism.
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires proxy/gateway configuration to be queryable via API confirming designated traffic is routed through authenticated proxies.

Mapping.rationale: SC-8 protects the confidentiality/integrity of data in transit; it does not address attack surface size or lateral-movement potential.

Mapping.prerequisites: Requires network/TLS scanning tooling that continuously verifies encryption is enforced on all transmission channels.

Mapping.prerequisites: Requires session-management configuration (load balancer/application) to be queryable via API for idle-timeout settings.

Mapping.rationale: SI-10 validates input to prevent injection-style attacks; it does not relate to network attack surface or lateral movement.

Mapping.rationale: SI-11 concerns limiting information disclosed in error messages; unrelated to attack surface or lateral movement.

Mapping.ai_description: An agentic AI code-review agent could semantically assess error-message content for information-disclosure risk across a codebase, going beyond static SAST rules.

Mapping.rationale: Memory protection reduces exploitability of a single compromised process, which has a loose connection to limiting lateral movement, but it's a very indirect link to network-level attack surface review.
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires OS/runtime configuration (e.g., ASLR, DEP flags) to be queryable via a configuration-scanning agent.

Mapping.rationale: Managed access control points for remote access are one mechanism supporting traffic limitation, though narrower than general inbound/outbound traffic configuration review.

Mapping.ai_description: Beyond static hardening-scan rules, an agentic AI could apply contextual judgment about whether a given open port/service is genuinely unnecessary and autonomously flag or disable it.

Mapping.rationale: Denying traffic by default and allowing only by exception directly matches 'limit inbound and outbound network traffic.'
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires firewall/security-group configuration to be queryable via API to confirm a default-deny posture with explicit exception rules.

Mapping.rationale: Spam is one form of 'other unwanted activity' named in the KSI, but SI-8 is narrower (email-specific) than the general protection-effectiveness review the KSI describes.
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires an email security gateway with API-queryable status and signature-update logs.

Mapping.rationale: This is a narrow maintenance detail (auto-updating spam signatures) and weak standalone evidence of a broader protections-effectiveness review.

Mapping.prerequisites: Requires network/TLS scanning tooling that continuously verifies encryption is enforced on all transmission channels.

Mapping.rationale: Social engineering training is a specific topic within general awareness training; relevant but narrower than the KSI's broader scope.

Mapping.rationale: This is a narrow, role-specific training requirement (PII processing) that only applies to a subset of staff; a small piece of the overall training landscape.

Mapping.ai_description: Same reasoning as AT-2: an agentic AI could review PII-handling training content for topic coverage.

Mapping.prerequisites: Same LMS/human-review prerequisite as other training controls; also requires an identified population of relevant personnel/supply-chain roles.
Mapping.ai_description: Same reasoning as AT-2: an agentic AI could review anti-counterfeit training content for topic coverage.

Mapping.rationale: Automatically disabling/removing temporary and emergency accounts after a defined period is a direct, core instance of automated account lifecycle management.

Mapping.rationale: Automatically disabling expired, orphaned, or policy-violating accounts is a direct, core instance of automated lifecycle management.

Mapping.rationale: Automatically disabling accounts of high-risk individuals is a direct, core instance of automated lifecycle/privilege management.

Mapping.rationale: Reviewing and adjusting assigned privileges directly matches the KSI's 'privileges... are securely managed' language.

Mapping.ai_description: Beyond running an access-certification campaign, an agentic AI could autonomously flag likely-excessive entitlements via role/usage-pattern analysis, closing the human-review gap.

Mapping.rationale: Managing user status identifiers is part of account lifecycle information, but it's a narrower labeling requirement, not full lifecycle/privilege management.

Mapping.rationale: Identity proofing occurs at initial account creation/registration; it's about verifying who a person is, not the ongoing lifecycle/privilege management of existing accounts.

Mapping.rationale: This is a narrow sub-requirement of identity proofing (presenting evidence), tangential to ongoing account lifecycle/privilege automation.

Mapping.rationale: Same identity-proofing family as above; tangential to ongoing lifecycle/privilege management.

Mapping.rationale: This is a narrow identity-proofing enhancement (address verification during enrollment); it has no connection to automated account lifecycle or privilege management.
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires an out-of-band verification service (SMS/mail) integrated into enrollment, with delivery/confirmation logged via API.

Mapping.rationale: AC-3 is the general access-enforcement control; it doesn't speak to authentication method (passwordless/MFA) specifically.

Mapping.ai_description: An agentic AI could cross-reference authenticator type to the documented sensitivity mapping across multiple systems autonomously, replacing what previously needed manual reconciliation.

Mapping.rationale: Obscuring authentication feedback (e.g., masking password entry) is a supporting detail, not central to the passwordless/MFA adoption decision.

Mapping.rationale: AC-2 governs the broader account-management lifecycle (types, approvals, etc.); it is not specific to authentication method selection.

Mapping.rationale: Automated temporary/emergency account handling is a direct instance of just-in-time access provisioning.

Mapping.rationale: Disabling accounts supports lifecycle hygiene generally but isn't specific to the JIT/role/attribute-based authorization model itself.
Mapping.prerequisites: Requires IAM/identity-governance automation triggered by HR/directory events (expiration, termination, policy violation) with API-queryable logs.

Mapping.rationale: This is an audit-logging requirement for account actions, evidentiary rather than part of the authorization model itself.

Mapping.rationale: Dynamic privilege management is a direct, core mechanism matching 'just-in-time' privilege assignment.

Mapping.ai_description: No change. An agentic AI could triage just-in-time access requests using richer context than a fixed PAM ruleset, but autonomously granting elevated privilege without a human gate carries meaningful risk.

Mapping.rationale: AC-3 is the core access-enforcement mechanism underlying the described authorization model.

Mapping.rationale: Restricting privileged accounts to specific individuals/roles directly matches the RBAC/least-privilege model described.

Mapping.rationale: Narrow scope (who can manage audit tooling), tangential to the broader authorization model.

Mapping.rationale: Configuration management planning is unrelated to the account/role authorization model.

Mapping.rationale: Identifier assignment is foundational but tangential to the authorization model's design.
